about: The bowed string instruments as a tree of types (registry/README.md): what is true of every bowed string at the top -- each string's pitch, density, impedance and stiffness from what was measured of it, by the physics' equations -- and below, each instrument's own. A value a node does not give is its parent's; `strings.*` a rule for each of a node's strings, read with that string's own values.

bowed-string-instrument.about: An instrument whose strings are bowed: made of its strings (a set of strings, a part of its own), its body and its bow.

violin-family.about: The violin, viola, cello and contrabass, and an instrument made like them.

tuning.note: its open strings, lowest first: its strings' pitches where it gives none

stringsAtOnce.note: the bridge's curvature and the bow's tension make it "not possible to sound more than two strings at the same time": a triple or quadruple stop arpeggiated (the violin's page; the family's bridges alike arched)

hairWidth.reason: the violin bow's measured width taken for every bow of the family: no viola, cello or bass bow's ribbon found measured (its rehairers set it by the bow's mortise and ferrule, bow by bow)

searched.query: bow hair ribbon width mm violin viola cello double bass
searched.found: retailers' bow lengths, weights and hair lengths; a museum bass bow's head 21.2 mm wide (University of Edinburgh MIMEd 17331); no ribbon width

searched.query: bow ferrule width mm violin cello bass hair ribbon width rehair specification
searched.found: a violin ribbon 10 to 12 mm by its ferrule (violinist.com forum); Arcus's hair cross-sections by bow, mm2 (violin 5-8, cello 9-13, bass 11-16), not widths; no larger bow's ribbon width

hairStiffness.note: the robot's cello bow's hair a spring in series with its contact, per metre of its ribbon's width, optimized against its attacks on string A with the string's torsion and elasto-plastic friction; taken for every bow of the family (no other measured)

hairDamping.note: the dashpot beside that spring, as it

r0.note: the losses a string has while the bow is on it beyond its own: string A's bowed less its plucked -- the torsion its friction drives and the hair's damping, which the engine does not model; one cello G string's, taken for every string of the family (none other measured)

static.note: rosined hair on a cello G string (Dominant), from its bridge force just before the first slip: "approximately 1.4" averaged over all their attacks, strongly dependent on the force, little on the acceleration (Galluzzo's 0.66 the measured span's other end); taken for every string of the family (no other measured), where Artifastring's tables drew theirs from 0.58 to 1.06

dynamic.note: the dynamic coefficient their limits took from the literature (Smith & Woodhouse 2000, "The tribology of rosin"); its drop from the static, 0.9, within the 0.6 at low force to 1 at high they measured at the first slip (4.1, Figure 11b)

steepness.reason: ours: the speed of slipping over which the friction falls from its static to its dynamic coefficient in Artifastring's hyperbola (its v0), within the 0.05 to 0.3 its tables were drawn from (Percival, Artifastring research/shared/published_constants.py); with it, the static and dynamic above and the hair and losses, the engine's attacks from rest on Lampis' string A met the robot's, 236 of its 859 within 20 periods to its 188 (Artifastring's contact 27) (native/strings-model/lampis_guettler.py, 7 November 2026)

searched.query: lampis-acta-2024: a friction curve's speed scale
searched.found: the coefficients at the first slip and averaged over 0.1 s, a quadratic in force and acceleration "solely as a visualization tool"; no curve against slipping speed
an elasto-plastic law (bristles, their stiffness and damping fitted) in place of a curve of slipping speed; no v0

solver.note: the bowed-string engine plays it on the solver and rates of the measured instrument whose lowest open string is nearest its own (itself where it is one)

bodyFrom.note: the measured body nearest it in its lowest air mode (itself where it is one), stretched in time to its own: interim, until its own is fitted

bodyRatio.note: how much longer in time the borrowed body's responses are played: its air mode over this one's

bowed-string-set.about: A set of strings for a bowed instrument: each string's pitch, impedance, stiffness and inharmonicity from its tension, density, length, modulus and diameter, by the physics' equations -- a rule for each of its strings, read with that string's own values.

strings-by-pitch.about: A set of strings given by their pitches, tensions and length (a maker's chart, a spec): each string's frequency from its pitch, its density from its tension, length and frequency, the steel cylinder of that density and the modulus that gives its stiffness.

diameter.note: the steel cylinder of the string's density, not a wound string's outer diameter: only E d^4 enters the model

given-strings.about: A set of strings given as data, nobody's measured: each string's stiffness and losses like the measured string nearest its pitch.

stiffness.note: the measured string nearest its pitch (Artifastring's first sets), the same string at its own length and tension: its stiffness EI

losses.note: that string's measured decays by frequency, read between them at its own modes (the contrabass's law r0 + r2 f^2, fitted to them, had left the first mode decaying at 46 to 51 /s where the measured strings' decay at 0.4 to 2)

contrabass-strings.about: The contrabass's strings, D'Addario Helicore orchestral 3/4 medium, as measured: their pitches, tensions and length from the maker's chart, their stiffness and losses fitted to another bass's recorded pizzicati -- and from those, by the equations, their density, inharmonicity, stiffness, the steel cylinder of their density and the modulus that gives that stiffness, and their losses' law r0 + r2 f^2.
